newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: AUSTRIA'S VRANITZKY SEES ITALY IN EMU AROUND 1999.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRIA'S VRANITZKY SEES ITALY IN EMU AROUND 1999.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said on Friday he expected Italy to join Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 or shortly thereafter.

"1999 would be ideal, and if it doesn't work in 1999 then it will be very soon thereafter," he told Reuters during a summit of eastern and central European leaders in the southern Austrian town of Graz.
"I am extremely interested that Italy will be among those countries that take part in EMU, if possible at the beginning, and if not at the beginning then very soon thereafter," he added.
Italy is Austria's second most important trading partner after Germany. Austria itself believes it will be among the first group of countries to join the single currency.

"There is some thinking in the European Union that the lira has to be sufficiently hard, but that's exactly where (Italian Prime Minister Romani Prodi) is making a great effort, which I fully support," Vranitzky said.
The Italian government aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire (42 billion) from the country's huge public debt to prepare for EMU.
Vranitzky was due to meet Prodi for bilateral talks later on Friday.
